verification.notes: The URL recorded in the assignment (…/international-vice-chancellors-scholarship-100-south-asia) returns 404, and a second likely variant URL also returns 404. Deakin's own scholarship search index, which holds 165 scholarship documents, contains exactly one international Vice-Chancellor's scholarship - the Deakin Vice-Chancellor's International Scholarship, status 'open', open-date display 'Trimester 3 2026', annual value display '100% or 50% of your tuition fees plus participation in the Vice-Chancellor's Professional Excellence Program and priority place in on-campus accommodation (at own cost and subject to availability)'. A query of that index for 'south asia' returns only three unrelated results, confirming the South Asia variant is no longer published. The record therefore records the current published award on Deakin's own page, and the South Asia-specific eligibility previously held in the catalogue (country residence, applying via a Deakin agent, 85%+ in Year 12) is flagged as not confirmed rather than carried forward.

applicant_utility.summary: Deakin has folded its country-specific international scholarships into a single Vice-Chancellor's International Scholarship, so do not plan around a dedicated South Asia round - the outcome is now either 100% or 50% of tuition fees and you will not know which until you are told. This one is genuinely application-based rather than automatic: unlike most of Deakin's international scholarships, it needs the International Scholarship Program form, a 300-word personal statement and two references, emailed to Deakin International Admissions at least a month before your program starts. The academic bar is at least an 85% average with several published reference points (85% overall in CBSE, ICSE or State Board Year 12; 10 overall in GCSE/A Level; 32 in the IB Diploma; or 80% across the first four semesters of an undergraduate degree), and Deakin warns that stronger results may be needed because competition is strong. Winning also commits you to the Vice-Chancellor's Professional Excellence Program, which is a requirement of the scholarship, not an optional extra.
applicant_utility.best_fit: New international coursework applicants with a consistently 85%+ academic record who are willing to write a personal statement, line up two references, and commit to the Vice-Chancellor's Professional Excellence Program.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your intended degree is not the Doctor of Medicine (H911), which is explicitly excluded
Work out which of Deakin's published equivalence points your result maps to (85% Year 12, 10 in GCSE/A Level, 32 IBDP, or 80% across the first four undergraduate semesters)
Draft the 300-word personal statement in your own words, covering why Deakin, extracurricular or work experience, and what makes you a strong ambassador
Ask referees early - you need two references specifically addressing community involvement and/or leadership, not just academic ability
Send the completed form and documents to Deakin International Admissions at least one month before your program start date
Check the English entry requirements on your specific degree page, since Deakin sets them per program
common_rejection_risks: Assuming this scholarship is automatic like most other Deakin international scholarships and never submitting the separate form
Being on the Doctor of Medicine (H911), which is excluded outright
Sitting on the application until the program start date is close, when the instruction is at least one month before
Submitting generic references that speak to grades rather than community involvement and leadership
Expecting a 100% outcome as standard when it is '100% or 50% depending on scholarship outcome'
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Any portion of tuition not covered if the outcome is the 50% tier, all living and accommodation costs (priority accommodation access is at your own cost), Overseas Student Health Cover, flights and visa costs, plus any fees for extra or repeated units and study beyond the standard program duration.
document_audit: The application is a PDF form emailed to International Admissions, not an online portal submission, so build in email delivery time
The personal statement has a hard 300-word limit - Deakin asks for it in your own words and your own voice
The two references must specifically highlight community involvement and/or leadership skills, so generic academic referees are a weak fit
The program application including academic transcripts must accompany the scholarship application
An interview may be part of the process, so keep your availability open after submission
alerts: Only successful applicants are contacted, so silence after submission is the expected outcome for most people rather than a system failure
Winning the scholarship obliges you to participate in the Vice-Chancellor's Professional Excellence Program
The accommodation benefit is priority access only, at your own cost and subject to availability - it is not free housing
The scholarship does not cover study beyond the standard program duration, including extra or repeated units, so a failed or repeated subject is on you
Because the country-specific variant has been withdrawn, older listings promising a dedicated South Asia 100% round should be treated as out of date
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply for a Deakin coursework degree, complete the International Scholarship Program form with a 300-word personal statement, two references and transcripts, and email the package to Deakin International Admissions at least a month before your program starts.
